text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with a chronic cough, weight loss, and weakness. To begin our evaluation, how long has your cough been persisting, and does it produce any sputum?

text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The combination of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and a chronic cough lasting 6 months is concerning. Given your recent release from prison, are you currently able to undergo any diagnostic tests today, such as a Chest X-Ray?

text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: The constellation of fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and a chronic cough lasting six months is highly suggestive of a systemic infection, particularly tuberculosis. Given your history of recent incarceration, this risk factor is significant. I need to confirm if you have been evaluated or treated by anyone else for these symptoms in the past year.
